findings.title: A stranger's deposit under the wallet's register is taken for the wallet's own unmixed box, and Mix my boxes again takes it first, tying the mix session and its private funding to that register
findings.scenario: Alice's Seedelf name resolves to a register R = (g, u) on chain, and anyone can read it. Mallory deposits one box into the v2 5 ₳ pool with datum (g^d, u^d), paid from her own address, which costs her 5 ₳ that Alice keeps. At Alice's next pool read, lovejoinOwned's key check (b = a^x) counts the box as Alice's. No record accounts for it, so found()/made() ask Koios. tx_info shows only Mallory's inputs, so the Origin is {mixed:false} with no `public` flag, and depositsOf holds the box as 'not mixed yet'. The page then says 'the server says a deposit put it into the pool, and no mix has moved it since … Mix my boxes again takes it first.' Alice presses Mix my boxes again, the action the wallet offers. againBoxes counts the box, because privately() drops only public accounts' boxes. fanOut sorts the not-mixed-yet boxes first, and WebAssembly mixes ours[..boxes], so the chain's first mix spends Mallory's box. Every one of Alice's other boxes that the chain takes goes in beside it. Every mix's fee and collateral come from the mix session's one-time account, and the funding paid that account from Alice's private UTxOs. Mallory watches her box get spent by a mix whose payer is that one-time account. From then on that account, the Seedelf inputs and change of its funding, and every other box of Alice's in that chain are tied to Alice's name. privacy.md says nothing of a box someone else puts in under your key. It admits only that a Mix again links its one-time account to its funding, with 'one of the three … likely yours'.
findings.since: 4498f935 (independent review M14: a deposit-made box no record accounts for is held as not mixed yet; ae8c2f33 had already made Mix again take not-mixed-yet boxes first), before web-wallet/1.0.0
findings.evidence:
1. The wallet's ownership check is the key check alone. wasm/src/lovejoin.rs:2605-2611 owned_in: `.filter_map(|row| PoolBox::from_row(row, &protocol)).partition(|b| b.is_owned(&sk))`, and PoolBox::from_row (seedelf-core/src/lovejoin/mod.rs:414-427) needs only the pool's value and a valid {a,b} with a≠b.
2. madeBy (lovejoin.ts:6252-6260) records only `mixed`, `mixedIn` and `public`, the last only from a public account's payment key. A stranger's deposit becomes {mixed:false}.
3. depositsOf (lovejoin.ts:2000-2007): `owned.filter((b) => !known(b) && mixedFor(origins[b.txHash], poolOf(b)) === false)`. notMixedYet (2010) = unmixedOf + depositsOf.
4. againBoxes (3501): `const owned = publicToo ? split.owned : this.privately(split.owned, …)`, and privately (3537-3540) removes only fromPublic. made() (3496) asks Koios first and then lets the box through as told.
5. fanOut (3786-3789): `left` = fromPublic + untold only. 3819-3834: `const unmixed = new Set(notMixedYet(schedule, owned).map(ref)); const first = (u) => (unmixed.has(outpoint(u)) ? 0 : 1);` … `pool: this.real(split).filter((u) => !left.has(outpoint(u))).sort((a, b) => first(a) - first(b))`.
6. wasm/src/lovejoin.rs:1587-1591 partitions request.pool in order. 1624-1635: `let payer = lovejoin::Payer { fee, collateral, address, signers: 1 }; lovejoin::again_at(…, &payer, &ours[..boxes], …)`. The session's address pays and backs every mix.
7. UI: Lovejoin.tsx:1290 NotMixed shows en.json:1272 'the server says a deposit put it into the pool, and no mix has moved it since' and 1259-1260 'Mix my boxes again takes it first.'
8. The behaviour is pinned today from the 'is it the account's?' angle only: tests/lovejoin-restore.test.ts:749-768. A deposit paid from `stranger = "ee".repeat(28)` is asserted `notMixed` and then `expect(await t.lovejoin.againBoxes("preprod", false, ADA)).toEqual({ boxes: 1, owned: 1 })` with the comment 'A deposit's box, mixed again from the private balance as any is.' I didn't run it; finders run nothing.
findings.fix: When Koios or the index says what made a box, tell the phrase's own deposits from anyone else's. madeBy would recognise an input under a one-time account's key (the session indexes the restore scan derives) or a public account's payment key as the wallet's. A deposit with neither is a stranger's, recorded as Origin `stranger`. Mix my boxes again would then leave such a box out, as it leaves fromPublic out, or mix it in a chain of its own. The NotMixed callout would say someone else put it in under your key. Bring it back anyway stays its way out: one withdraw ties only what a received payment ties. The same class covers every place that puts boxes of different makings into one payer's chain: Mix again with `publicToo` (no lookup at all), and bootstrapOf, which holds boxes of unknown making in a Bootstrap's place. lovejoin-restore.test.ts:749's expectation changes with the fix.
findings.owner_why: It changes what Mix my boxes again takes and what the not-mixed-yet callout offers, and it sorts a deposit box into 'yours' or 'someone else's'.
findings.known_check: Searched backlog.md (Lovejoin section, Declined, every ❓/⬜) and every file under docs/archive/plans/ for: stranger, dust, plant, 'deposit under', 'someone else's deposit', 'box someone else put', 're-randomized … box', 'attacker'. Read M14's row and plan in independent-review.md, privacy-review.md §2.10, and privacy.md's Lovejoin, Co-spending and Several public accounts sections. All of them treat a box no record accounts for as the wallet's own, a restore's or another device's. None considers one deposited by someone else under the wallet's key. chunk-34's spam section is about pools, not boxes.

guards.stops: evaluable/withinDepth (2722): a session UTxO with a reference script or an over-deep datum counted as holding a token the deposit takes (a way that takes no box), and a recursive walk a datum thousands of levels deep would trap
reserve(): two chains spending one pool box or input (StalePool, rebuilt avoiding them), the collateral tail's two draws included
a chain's reservation is taken before the network's check and let go when that check refuses it (also acrossOf 4098-4102), so no other chain draws its boxes meanwhile

withdrawDueNow sends no withdraw while Mix again (6793) or a chain (6796) is mixing, or while the last withdraw may have gone (6798): a box withdrawn under a chain that spends it, or two withdraws of one box
guards.test: tests/lovejoin-withdraw-submit.test.ts (133-333); none found pinning 6793/6796 by name

guards.stops: never withdraws a box a built or sending chain reserved (free(inPool(back, pool), reserved)); back already excludes held boxes (not mixed yet, unsure, untold, a Bootstrap's, a tail's)
a withdraw whose hash changed between build and the signed transaction (giveme.my or signing altered it) is never sent

the withdraw is kept sealed and its box held as spent before the submit, so a lock, a closed browser or a stopped worker never forgets a withdraw that may have gone (M1). A lock before the submit marks it refused (neverWent, then dropRefused restores its due time, F5)
tells a refusal (box freed, due time back) from a submit that may have gone (5xx, timeout, KoiosBusyError.maybeSent), which stays looked for and is never rebuilt into a second spend of the box
takesNewBoxes/usableNow (4198): a new box in a retired pool, a copy, or a pool whose box is below the network's minimum, before anything is funded or built
crossCheck: a chain whose first mix (each pool's first, across pools) the network measures above its declared budget or refuses is never sent, which would risk the collateral
chainRetryMs: a chain's first transaction refused as spent isn't retried unless a try may have sent it; later ones retry CHAIN_SPENT_TRIES times
adaPoolOf: a return's ADA and collateral go only into a shown v2 5 ₳ ADA pool, never a copy or a retired pool
poolChoice: a page's pool choice for a return's tokens is kept only for a well-formed unit and pool id (anything else is dropped); acrossOf takes a named pool only if it's among those that work now
attempt(): a chain whose pool has too few free others for its width is skipped, never built short

a data-layer pool whose reference UTxO, scripts and launch aren't one transaction isn't built on; verified() (530) refuses inline scripts and unlisted values; holder() refuses launches younger than SETTLE_MS (572-581) and pools whose L isn't registered by the launch or an earlier block (632)

checked_ok: withinDepth (lovejoin.ts:2722) matches core's cbor::walk (seedelf-core/src/cbor.rs:19-123) branch for branch. Text strings are UTF-8-checked per chunk, as minicbor 0.25.1's str_iter does. A break must end an indefinite container. A map's count overflows to refusal. The depth is checked before an empty container. Trailing bytes are refused. Info 28-30 and an info of 31 on majors 0/1/6 are refused, as minicbor's type_of does. The walk is linear, with no recursion. The vectors test holds it.
evaluable (2706) mirrors core's eval::refusal/unreadable_datum: a reference script is refused, hex that won't parse reads as no datum, and anything else goes through within_depth.

secureRandom (1791) draws 53 uniform bits from crypto.getRandomValues. draw() (5485) spreads each box uniformly over its delay's range from its first transaction's send, and a recorded delay (a swap's approved one) overrides Settings'.

unlockWait (1738) stays within [2 min, min(20 min, auto-lock − 2 min)]. unlockDraws (6961) redraws, once an unlock, each due time that falls within 2 minutes, and the maybe-sent withdraw's resend too. The unlock's own run sends nothing (6845).

The five-minute quiet rule: withdrawDueNow sends nothing in a run that sent anything else (6902). It pushes a box within QUIET_AFTER_SEND_MS of the last send or a forgotten one (6904-6911), at most QUIET_PUSHES times. resends() (7892) ignores the withdraw's own last send.

One box a run: every other due time already due gets a fresh WITHDRAW_SPREAD_MS draw before the withdraw is built (6926-6935). A box goes only once it has waited Settings' least since its last move and its own chain's least (ripeAt); otherwise its due time moves past the first that will (6893-6896).

Maybe-sent withdraws: the record is kept before rememberSpent and the submit. A lock in between is handled by refused/dropRefused. A lock-wiped spent set is held again in settleWithdrawing (7833-7836). A withdraw unseen after SPENT_KEEP_MS is dropped, and its box gets a fresh due time from scheduleFound. One that lands is written to the history with its ties/origin, as withdrawOne would have.

Reservations: reserve() keeps no two chains on one input, and reservationOf covers every transaction of a chain, the tail's mix and its draws included. split/splitAll draw only from boxes no other chain reserved (`except` the owner's own) and never from a Bootstrap's held box (real() is owned∪others).

Retired pools: isRetired (classic plus every non-v2 pool) is refused before anything is read, in usableNow/takesNewBoxes. adaPoolOf, poolsOf(unit), usable() and acrossOf's tokenPools all leave retired pools and copies out. chain() turns a return or a Mix again into a retired pool into LovejoinSkipped. sortOut holds nothing in a retired pool but a box of a chain still being sent.

Reward balance: rewardsIn reads each pool once a build (`known` survives unstale's tries and four's fall to three). balancesOf/readsFor name only the accounts the transactions withdraw from. withdrawOne rebuilds once on RewardsChangedError, with its due time back in between. The races left are the backlog's ❓ (backlog.md:56-60).

M14 look-up: found() asks only when the count can't account for the boxes, or of a transaction still being asked of. made() asks of one box before it's taken. madeBy names an account only by a payment key; a stake key alone leads to fartherKeys, bounded by FARTHER_KEYS. inputsOf never asks the data layer about the wallet's own boxes. A Koios failure keeps the transaction in `asking` and its boxes held. Kupo's null inputs are temporary.

pumpChain (462): no more than its window waits in the mempool. It asks giveme.my only once nothing is in flight. After CHAIN_RESEND_MS it resends everything in flight, in order. A spent refusal with the parent still in flight triggers one resend and then stops (resentFor). A send cut short stays maybe-sent (`sending`).

Figures: mixesPerBox, chainBoxes and MAX_CHAIN_MIXES = 130 give 32 boxes at two waves, 10 at three and 64 for a v2 deposit, as privacy.md says. roomLeavingTail leaves the tail its two draws, except where one box is all that fits, as documented.

lovejoin-pools.ts: shown() keys on set and values and doesn't depend on order (object identity holds for rule.includes). A pool handed over stays as a copy for good. Writes to the record are serialised per network (serially). A launch younger than SETTLE_MS keeps the next look's height below its block. An L registration counts only before the launch's block (`<` on block times, both in seconds).

poolRows: the data layer's combined feed is split per pool by each row's payment credential. A pool the feed doesn't cover falls back to Koios in one request. Provenance is kept only for pools the index covered, so Koios is asked about the rest.
notes: For the UI lane (E8a), known in part: 'Pay from my private balance anyway' (againBoxes/fanOut with publicToo, lovejoin.ts:3496, 3501, 3788) takes every public account's boxes. It also skips the M14 look-up entirely, so a box no record accounts for goes in unasked. The modal (en.json lovejoin.privateAnyway.privacy.ties) and the review (lovejoin.review.privacy.publicToo) say 'your public account' and 'that account'. With boxes from Accounts 1 and 2, one one-time account pays for both, which ties the two accounts to each other as well as to the private balance, and the words name neither. privacy.md documents that it 'still takes every account's, after its warning'. But its Several public accounts rule says a review names the accounts.

Stale comment (nit): the header's request list (lovejoin.ts:75-88) gives a withdraw as 'giveme.my plus one submit'. Since chunk 43 it also reads the pool's mix_logic account_info (rewardsIn, 7572), and a token pool's due box reads the epoch parameters (6867). privacy.md has it right.

A doubt, not traced to a concrete gain: due times are slots shared by the whole pool. Where chains with different recorded delays share a pool, a slot that comes up before any candidate is ripe moves to that candidate's least + 5-60 min (6894-6895). So a longer-delay chain's boxes cluster just after their least rather than spreading over the approved range. This is a side of F9's fix, not something it got wrong.

Harmless: at an auto-lock of 4 minutes or less, unlockWait's range is [2 min, 2 min], so every redrawn due time lands on the same millisecond. moveDue then shares or deletes one marks entry among the equal times. One still goes a run and the rest spread again.

A narrow race, not reported: withdrawDueNow passes the mixingAgain check (6793) and then waits on giveme.my. If a Mix again funding is submitted, lands and has its chain built before the withdraw's rememberSpent, the chain's first mix can draw the box being withdrawn. Only a phase-1 refusal follows (the mix session's two fees), and the timing needs giveme.my to be slow.

The same class as e1a#1: bootstrapOf (2549-2564) holds boxes of unknown making in place of a Bootstrap's moved boxes, so a stranger's planted box can stand in for one. That box is then held, not mixed.

A retired pool's unknown boxes are still looked up with Koios (found → moreThanDue with retired=true) although sortOut doesn't hold them there. The answer still feeds depositAccountOf's ties (PRIV-3), so it isn't wasted.
